where: figure (Account files written by useradd): shadow node note and aria text
problem: The figure says useradd writes a 'password hash, lock flag' to /etc/shadow. useradd never writes a real hash; it writes a locked placeholder such as ! or * until passwd is run. This contradicts the chapter's own sentence in Section 2: 'useradd does not set a password. The new account stays locked until passwd puts a hash in shadow.'
fix: Change the shadow node note to 'locked placeholder (!), no hash yet' and the aria to '... a locked password placeholder to /etc/shadow (a real hash is written only later by passwd)'.

where: figure (Account files written by useradd): group node note and edge from useradd
problem: The figure shows useradd writing ravi's membership with GID 2000 into /etc/group. With useradd -g students, the primary GID is stored only in field 4 of /etc/passwd; useradd does not add ravi to the member list of an existing group. Section 1 of the chapter states this correctly, so the figure contradicts the text.
fix: Remove the useradd → /etc/group edge (or label it 'created earlier by groupadd -g 2000 students'), and show that the member list of /etc/group is updated only later, by usermod -aG project ravi in the worked example.

problem: Saying 'groupdel project deletes an empty group' suggests groupdel refuses groups that have members. In fact groupdel deletes a group even when users list it as a supplementary group; it refuses only when the group is some user's primary group.
fix: groupdel project deletes the group record, as long as no user has project as a primary group; it also removes project from users' supplementary lists.

problem: 'userdel ravi removes the passwd, shadow and group entries' can be read as deleting the students/project groups, which userdel never does.
fix: userdel ravi removes ravi's lines from /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow and removes ravi from the member lists in /etc/group; the group records themselves stay.
